name: How do luxury builders handle privacy and security features?

mainEntity.name: What privacy and security features should be planned into a high-end custom home from the start?
mainEntity.text: What privacy and security features should be planned into a high-end custom home from the start?

acceptedAnswer.text: Privacy and security should be part of the design phase, not added at the end. In luxury homes, the best results come when architecture, landscaping, lighting, and technology are planned together. That can include gate placement, entry sequencing, camera and alarm prewiring, fencing, sightline control, and strategic window placement. For homes in denser neighborhoods like Westwood, Studio City, or Beverly Hills, privacy often matters as much as aesthetics. The builder should coordinate these features with the electrician, low-voltage contractor, and designer so the house feels secure without looking fortified. Homeowners should also think about guest circulation, service access, and garage entry so the property functions smoothly. Planning these items early usually costs less and produces a cleaner finished result than retrofitting later.
acceptedAnswer.description: Privacy and security features should be planned early so they can be integrated into the architecture, landscaping, and electrical systems. Common examples include controlled entry, gated access, camera prewiring, protected sightlines, layered landscaping, and window placement that reduces visibility. Retrofitting these features later is usually more expensive and less effective.
